method.method_draft: Read the image as a polar region whose shaded set R starts at the pole, is swept out from the positive x-axis up to the diagonal ray, and has its outer boundary on the curve. From the text, use the ray θ = π/4 and the polar curve r = 2 cos θ + sin θ. Since the first-quadrant shaded region corresponds to angles 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/4 and radii 0 ≤ r ≤ 2 cos θ + sin θ, apply the polar area formula A = ∫ (1/2) r_outer^2 dθ. This gives ∫_0^{π/4} (1/2)(2 cos θ + sin θ)^2 dθ, equivalently the standard form ∫_0^{π/4} r^2/2 dθ with r = 2 cos θ + sin θ.
